phase_0.boundary_condition: The SIXTEEN_3 powerset carrier P({T,F,t,f}) containing all 16 subsets under three interlocking orders

⊢.justification: The void state {} representing no constructive proof, refutation, or information; the bottom of the information order

⊣.justification: The closed boundary containing all 16 values; the top of the information order where all four base values are present

≻.justification: Forward morphism along the truth order ≤_t, increasing constructive proof or acceptable truth while decreasing falsity

≺.justification: Reverse morphism swapping T↔F and t↔f simultaneously; the internal negation that preserves information content while inverting truth polarity

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of lattice operations where the output of one ordering feeds into the next, maintaining structural integrity across ≤_t, ≤_f, and ≤_i

⊙.justification: Identity mapping where the lattice value recognizes itself; the neutral element that preserves the current subset without transformation

∈.justification: Co-multiplication δ that decomposes a value into three independent arms: constructive truth (T), constructive falsity (F), and information layer (t,f)

∋.justification: Multiplication μ that reconstitutes the three arms into a single subset; conflicting arms (T and F) fuse to the B state without explosion

⊤.justification: Evaluation of the T-axis; asserts constructive truth by setting the big_t bit in the register

⊥.justification: Evaluation of the F-axis; asserts constructive falsity by setting the big_f bit in the register

⊞.justification: Simultaneous holding of both truth and falsity; enters the B state where contradiction is a legitimate resolution rather than an error

⊡.justification: Irreversible fixation of the current lattice state; appends the subset to the permanent record and prevents further modification

phase_3.void_description: The empty set {} with no bits set; no proof, no refutation, no information

phase_3.false_description: The subset {F} or {F,f} representing constructive refutation or rejectable falsity
phase_3.both_description: The subset {T,F} or {T,F,t,f} representing a dialetheia where truth and falsity are simultaneously held

steps.domain_action: Initialize the register to the empty set {} representing the void state before any lattice operations
Decompose the initial state into three independent arms for constructive truth, constructive falsity, and information layer
Evaluate the constructive truth arm by setting the big_t bit to assert proven truth
Propagate the truth value forward along the ≤_t order to increase constructive content
Compose the truth propagation with the next lattice operation to maintain structural continuity
Evaluate the constructive falsity arm by setting the big_f bit to assert refuted falsity
Apply the bilattice involution to swap T↔F and t↔f while preserving information content
Hold both truth and falsity simultaneously in the B state as a legitimate dialetheic resolution
Apply self-reference to the current state to recognize the lattice value without transformation
Reconstitute the three arms into a single subset where conflicting T and F arms fuse to B
Irreversibly commit the fused state to the permanent record as an immutable lattice value
Decompose the committed state again to explore alternative lattice configurations
Re-evaluate the truth arm with new constructive evidence
Re-evaluate the falsity arm with new refutational evidence
Maintain the dialetheic holding of both states as the system explores the full powerset
Rejoin the arms to form a new resolved subset reflecting the updated evidence
Fix the new state permanently to the record as the next step in the lattice evolution
Close the system boundary by containing all 16 possible subsets within the full lattice
